# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Parent = seed (both cand_0001 and cand_0002 were REJECTED and reverted). Root lesson from
the two rejections: each netted a POSITIVE Δ and fixed 53161, but each REGRESSED one passing
task (cand_0001 broke 160-6, cand_0002 broke 40467) and the gate rejects on any protected
regression. The regressions trace to TYPE-COERCION prose, not to breadth: "write real dates
not string forms" broke 160-6 (its date column is TEXT), and a "print & confirm Python TYPE
(int-vs-float / date-vs-text)" verify checklist misfires on 40467 (answer is intentionally
`str`) and 160-6 (mixed int/float + text dates). This iteration ships the SAME real fixes but
excises ALL type-coercion / verify-type language.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | anchored row-deletion | 347-49 (0.00, 3 trials) | wrong deletion rule: t0 deletes only all-blank rows (keeps label+header rows); t1 pastes VBA macro TEXT into cells; t2 keeps the marker row itself (off-by-one). Also str/int-where-float from dtype=object round-trip | KNOWLEDGE + CAPABILITY-GAP (method) | worked-example procedure (task_template) + "perform op, don't write code text" rule (prompt) |
| 2 | live-read / don't-overwrite | 52216 (0.22), + 53161 (0.67) | hardcodes preview values (caps 1/3) or shifts label→row mapping and overwrites the already-correct row | KNOWLEDGE | narrowing rule: compute from live file + change only cells the instruction asks (prompt) + cross-copy section (task_template) |
| 3 | read cached formula values | 374-9 (0.22) | plain openpyxl reads a col-H `=SUM()` cell as its formula STRING → float() skips it → every A-sum too low (0/3); data_only/pandas lifts it to the defect-capped 1/3 | KNOWLEDGE | missing-rule: read computed values via data_only/pandas (prompt) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 347-49 | missing-rule (grounded) | prompt.md | "graded artifact is DATA not source code — if asked for a macro/VBA/script/code, perform it and write only results". General to any "write me code" phrasing | yes — 160-6 ALSO says "I need a macro" and already passes by performing it; rule reinforces that. 40467/160-6 don't paste code |
| 347-49 | worked example / ordered procedure | task_template.md | scoped anchor-deletion procedure: delete the whole separator (blank + label + header rows), walk dynamically to the previous data row, match any example range, use openpyxl (not dtype=object) | yes — HARD-GATED on "instruction anchors deletion on a marker text"; explicitly says plain "remove blank rows" → delete only blanks (that IS 160-6, which stays unchanged) |
| 374-9 | missing-rule | prompt.md | read source with data_only=True/pandas for sums/lookups; formula cells else read as strings and get dropped; recompute None | yes — bounded to reads-for-aggregation; 40467-t1 already uses data_only; 160-6 copies literals (data_only leaves literals/text unchanged) |
| 52216 | decision-narrowing | prompt.md | compute from live file (no hardcoded preview values/indices) AND within answer_position change ONLY cells the instruction asks — leave already-correct/unmentioned cells at original value | yes — 40467 & 160-6 fill every cell their instruction requires; the "leave unmentioned cells" clause is inert on them |
| 52216/53161 | cross-copy framing | task_template.md | re-add proven "final block re-run on 3 copies → compute dynamically, locate by header/extent" section | yes — this exact section fixed 53161 in BOTH prior runs and never appeared in any broke={} |
| type-safety (protective) | type-preservation (NON-coercing) | prompt.md | "preserve values in native form; don't stringify (avoid dtype=object); copy date-like TEXT as text; do NOT convert text to dates or add rounding" | yes — this is the OPPOSITE of the clause that broke 160-6; it explicitly keeps text-dates as text (160-6-protective) and helps 347-49's str-where-float |
| verify | contract (no type language) | task_template.md | verify step now also confirms "no cell changed outside answer_position; unmentioned cells keep original value" — NO Python-type printing/int-vs-float/date-vs-text checks | yes — deliberately omits the type checklist that broke 40467 |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes on those exact inputs)
- 347-49 t1 pasted a 22-line `Sub DeleteBlankRowsAboveGrossPay()` macro into A1:A22 → prompt rule "if asked for a macro/VB code, perform it, don't write code text; a cell containing `Sub ...` is always wrong" would have made it execute the deletion instead. (1536/1536 mismatch → performs real op.)
- 347-49 t2 dropped Excel rows 29–35 but KEPT row 36 (the marker "Gross Pay" row) because its loop started at `idx-1` → worked example "note whether the marker row itself falls in the example range (29–36) and must be deleted too; walk to the previous genuine data row, don't stop at first non-blank" fixes the off-by-one and the "Employee Info" label retention.
- 347-49 t0 deleted only all-blank rows (kept label+header) → worked example "the separator often ALSO contains a label row and a repeated header row — delete the whole block" addresses it; anchored condition means 160-6 (no marker) is untouched.
- 374-9 t0 read `load_workbook(input_path)` (no data_only) → B7=1086469 (col-H formula string skipped); t1/t2 with data_only/pandas → 3834386 (correct, 1/3). Prompt rule forces the data_only path → 0/3 → defect-capped 1/3.
- 52216 t1 read live but shifted mapping, overwriting the already-correct Advertising row 15 (10/10 differ); t0/t2 hardcoded preview and needlessly overwrote C15 (capped 1/3). Rule "compute from live file + change ONLY the cells the instruction asks, leave already-correct cells" targets both; instruction itself states "the first row returns the correct values, as desired".
- 53161: cross-copy section is the exact text that produced fixed={53161} in cand_0001 AND cand_0002 per LEDGER — re-applied verbatim-in-spirit, minus the poison clauses.

## Blast-radius per edit (SAFE test)
- All edits are ADDITIVE or NARROWING (a stated condition present only in failing cases), no global decision/permission rule was loosened. Passing class enumerated: 40467 (Cell-Level, writes literal text from dates) and 160-6 (Sheet-Level, verbatim value shift, macro-worded, text-dates). Each edit checked against both: none changes what the agent DOES on either (see table "protects passing?"). The anchor-deletion example is hard-gated on a marker condition 160-6 lacks; NO type/verify-type clause is present.

## Process & features used
- Subagents: 3 parallel general-purpose read-only diagnosis agents (passing-task fragility; 347-49 deletion; flaky 374-9/52216/418-29) to read the raw traces and quote code, keeping diagnosis grounded rather than trusting the summary.
- Prior iterations read: cand_0001 + cand_0002 PROCESS.md + diff.patch (RUNMAP), LEDGER, full JOURNAL, and both auto-memory files (libreoffice-recalc-active, spreadsheetbench-ground-truth-data). Learned: which exact clauses regressed which task, and that cross-copy framing is the proven-safe 53161 fix.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- Do NOT add any verify-step that prints/asserts Python TYPE (int vs float, date vs text) — it breaks 40467 (text answer) and 160-6 (text dates / mixed int-float).
- Do NOT add "write real dates instead of string forms" — breaks 160-6 (text date column).
- Do NOT switch the global "prefer literals" rule to "write formulas" — regressed 52216 & 53161 (formulas score all-or-nothing on recalc; literals earn partial credit).
- KEEP the cross-copy "3 copies" section — proven to fix 53161 twice, no attributed regression.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 32468 (0.00): CORRUPTED GOLD (DISCOUNT!row2508 = 6.5 in every input but −7 in every answer; cell-level all-or-nothing) — unwinnable by any method. Handed back, no edit.
- 55457, 47484: infrastructure noise (55457 = empty instruction field; both mostly abort with sandbox/run errors, mean ~0). Not capability failures.
- 418-29 (0.33): its two 0-trials are sandbox exec TIMEOUTS (infra), not behavior; the one real trial (t2) is a 1-cell float-where-int near-miss on other variants. The only lever left is int-vs-float type coercion — the exact poison that broke 40467/160-6 — so I did NOT add a type rule for it. The generic non-coercing "don't stringify / no unrequested rounding" prompt line covers the safe part.
